study: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of generated answers across four retrieval configurations
source_note: Raw evidence is private (company-owned corpus and logs) and is not published.
what_it_measures: A calibrated LLM judge graded generated answers for 159 questions per retrieval configuration (arm) on seven dimensions (completeness, grounding, citation locality, calibration, language, source qualification, dialogue context) plus an overall fully-accepted label.
what_it_does_not_show: A winner. On the 157 questions graded in every arm, no pairwise difference in full acceptance is clear (exact McNemar p between 0.08 and 0.75). Judgments are model grades on exposed development and diagnostic cases, not human gold; the judge model also generated the answers. This study used an earlier hosted configuration, not the current runtime. The completion run used the same model name a day or two later; a provider-side model change in between cannot be ruled out.

logical_evaluation_coverage.interpretation: Shared reviews bind to several arms, so per-arm counts sum to 636 logical evaluations (367 valid, 267 quota-rejected, 2 inconsistent) while unique judge requests sum to 549.

completion_run.graded: the 242 judge requests the first run lost to HTTP 429 spend-limit rejections
completion_run.contract: same model, prompt, schema, reasoning effort none, 3,000 completion tokens and semantic validator; request hashes verified unchanged
completion_run.not_regraded: the 2 internally inconsistent first-run grades stay invalid (no outcome retries)

paired_comparison.note: Questions with a valid grade in all four arms. Dimension counts give pass, fail and not_applicable.

calibration.limits: References are agent adjudications, not independent human gold; agreement cells were not independently revalidated.

first_run_returned_token_usage.note: Quota-rejected requests returned no usage. Monetary billing was not accessed.

arm_ids_note: Arm 117ca79fe094e5ba is a configuration hash from the retrieval lab.
